rationale: This study is a cluster-randomised controlled trial (experimental design) across 332 rural villages (121 clusters) in the Democratic Republic of Congo evaluating the national Healthy Villages and Schools (VEA) community-driven WASH programme. On the mechanism side, the rule-governed institutional component centers on participation_assistance: communities must collectively decide to participate and sign an agreement with the Health Zone, elect and train a village WASH committee, receive 3-6 months of government/NGO facilitation and village-level infrastructure grants, and meet seven WASH/committee norms for certification. On the outcome side, multiple outcome families are co-equally central: the four preregistered primary outcomes span primary_connection (household coverage/use of an improved water source—on which trial power calculations were anchored—and improved sanitation facility) and effective_access (time spent collecting water and water quantity collected), alongside secondary outcomes measuring administrative_outcome (village water governance index), effective_access (functional water points, water satisfaction), and economic_access (financial cost of water).
